needs_review.issue: Wave n flagged two Youth Apostles seminarians as possibly centrally funded rather than personally support-raised - partially resolved
needs_review.finding: Three Youth Apostles were ordained priests by Bishop Burbidge on 2026-06-06: Eric McDade YA, Jim Harbour YA and Sean Mazary YA. All three are CONSECRATED members of Youth Apostles, not missionaries in the two-year fundraising program. Youth Apostles' own vocations page states that consecrated priests and consecrated laymen make promises of poverty, chastity and obedience and live consecrated life together in community houses.
needs_review.evidence: https://www.youthapostles.org/blog/vocations ; https://www.youthapostles.org/vocations ; Diocese of Arlington post describing Sean Mazary as 'a consecrated member of the Youth Apostles community and former Youth Missionary at Holy Trinity Catholic Church'
needs_review.recommendation: Treat consecrated members (priests and lay brothers) as Tier B / not ICP: a promise of poverty plus community living is inconsistent with managing a personal donor base. This most likely identifies the two flagged people as McDade and Mazary. NOT fully confirmed - no page states outright that consecrated members do or do not support-raise. Jim Harbour is already held and should have his tier re-checked on the same grounds. A fetch-enabled pass on /vocations and /support would settle it.

needs_review.issue: Office and program staff tiering is unresolved and I have deliberately NOT graded them on job function alone
needs_review.finding: Youth Apostles documents fundraising training only for Missionaries ('Missionaries are trained in how to fundraise to support their missionary service'). The Office Staff page lists a General Director, a Director of Mission and Development, a Development Officer and a Director of Communications, with no support ask visible in any snippet. Separately, Tyler Fabian (Development Officer) DOES have a root-level person page of the same shape the Missionaries use, which cuts the other way and suggests office staff may have support pages too.
needs_review.recommendation: Kieran Koch, Liz Garcia, Chris Hitzelberger and Tom Yehl are emitted Tier B provisionally on absence of evidence, not on job title. If a fetch of /officestaff shows per-person support asks, promote all four to Tier A. Do not bulk-grade either way without fetching one office-staff person page.

needs_review.issue: The /missionaries hub names placements but withholds the individual names from search snippets - this is where the remaining volume is
needs_review.finding: The Missionaries page is structured as: an Advisor to the Missionary Program, then missionaries grouped by placement at Bishop O'Connell Catholic High School, St. Paul VI Catholic High School and Holy Trinity Catholic Church, then Summer Missionaries. Every snippet returned the group headings and never the person names. Only Austin Mee (Bishop O'Connell) could be tied to a placement, and only via a separate query. The Advisor is named on the page but the name never appeared in any snippet.
needs_review.evidence: https://www.youthapostles.org/missionaries (surfaced in 8 of 18 queries, always with placement headings and never with person names)
needs_review.recommendation: HIGHEST-VALUE FOLLOW-UP: one page fetch of /missionaries almost certainly yields the full current missionary roster with root-level slugs, and these are the genuine Tier A records. Search alone cannot get at it. Do not buy another search-only slice on this domain for the missionary roster.

needs_review.issue: Root-slug enumeration is confirmed defeated on this domain, and the one alternative prefix is a dead end
needs_review.finding: As briefed, root-level slugs give the engine no prefix to walk. The literal title-suffix strings '| Youth Apostles' and ', YA | Youth Apostles' both returned only program and hub pages - zero person pages - because the suffix appears in the title of EVERY page on the site, person or not, so it has no discriminating power. The role-word, school-name and diocesan-context axes worked better and produced every new name in this file. I also found a second URL shape not previously recorded, the WordPress-style author archive /author/<slug> (e.g. /author/jlilly/page/2), but two queries against that prefix surfaced exactly one author.
needs_review.evidence: Coverage rows 1, 5, 17 and 18 (title-suffix and /author/ sweeps, all no_people); rows 4, 8, 9, 10, 16 (role/school/diocese axes, all found_people)
needs_review.recommendation: Retire the title-suffix tactic for Youth Apostles - it is structurally useless here, not just unlucky. The last three queries returned nothing new, so I stopped on budget and on the exhaustion signal simultaneously. Any further Youth Apostles work should be fetch-based against /missionaries, /officestaff and /ourcouncil rather than search-based. Also note /ourcouncil exists as a third named hub (General Director John More, council elected 2025-2028) whose member names never surfaced in snippets.
